root_cause.text: A race in cfg80211 PMSR teardown allowed the asynchronous work item `wdev->pmsr_free_wk` scheduled by `cfg80211_release_pmsr()` to remain pending while `cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down()` directly aborted requests during interface shutdown, so the work could later call the driver's `abort_pmsr` on an already torn-down `wireless_dev`.
root_cause.evidence: The CVE/commit states that `cfg80211_release_pmsr()` “schedules pmsr_free_wk to process the abort asynchronously,” while concurrent teardown makes `cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down()` call `cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort()` directly, and the patch fixes this by adding `cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk);` before the abort path to drain pending/in-progress work.

intent_record.intent_summary: Cancel pending PMSR free work during wireless device shutdown to avoid races with deferred cleanup during teardown.
intent_record.what: A call to cancel_work_sync(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk) was inserted in cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down() after releasing wdev->pmsr_lock and before the conditional call to cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(wdev).
intent_record.how: At runtime, this synchronously cancels any pending or running pmsr_free_wk work item before continuing shutdown handling, preventing that deferred work from executing concurrently or after the wireless device is being torn down and avoiding possible use-after-free or shutdown race issues.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it cancels the pending `pmsr_free_wk` during wireless device shutdown, preventing deferred PMSR cleanup from running after teardown and calling `abort_pmsr` on an already torn-down `wireless_dev`.

candidates.rationale: This direct abort during wireless device shutdown is the operation that races with the still-pending asynchronous pmsr_free_wk. Without first cancelling pending free work, this call can participate in teardown ordering that later lets deferred work invoke abort_pmsr on an already torn-down wireless_dev.

vuln_statements.explanation: During wireless device shutdown, this directly aborts PMSR requests without first cancelling any pending asynchronous pmsr_free_wk work. That leaves a race where the deferred work can later run and invoke the driver's abort path on an already torn-down wireless_dev.

commit 73350424bec9c76cf42d4d502ff156c7d5daf191
Author: Johannes Berg <johannes.berg@intel.com>
Date:   Wed Feb 6 08:03:10 2019 +0200

    cfg80211: pmsr: fix abort locking
    
    When we destroy the interface we already hold the wdev->mtx
    while calling cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down(), which assumes this
    isn't true and flushes the worker that takes the lock, thus
    leading to a deadlock.
    
    Fix this by refactoring the worker and calling its code in
    cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down() direc
bic_trace_step.reason: The diff shows the relevant teardown/abort logic completely enough to decide. The root cause was that asynchronous work `wdev->pmsr_free_wk` could remain pending while `cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down()` separately aborted requests, allowing later execution on a torn-down `wireless_dev`. In this commit, the abort logic was refactored into `static void cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(struct wireless_dev *wdev)`, and `cfg80211_pmsr_wdev_down()` no longer schedules the async worker. Specifically, the old code `if (found) schedule_work(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk); flush_work(&wdev->pmsr_free_wk);` was replaced with `if (found) cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(wdev);`. That means shutdown now performs the abort synchronously under the current `wdev->mtx` instead of relying on pending work. The worker `cfg80211_pmsr_free_wk()` still exists, but it now only locks `wdev`, calls `cfg80211_pmsr_process_abort(wdev)`, and unlocks, so the actual abort path is centralized and safe. Because the problematic construct of leaving teardown dependent on scheduled async work is absent here, `has_bug` is false, and because the synchronous direct call is the fix, `is_fixed` is true.
